name: Components
blurb: C4 level 3: what a domain team actually writes, and what the platform's own libraries do with it. Every box here is FLEX code — this is the product the platform ships to its domain teams.
audience: Domain teams — this is the part you write
note: Two files ship a route: domains/{name}/domain.config.ts and one handler file whose path toHandlerPath derives from the route key. Route counts live on Resources, log retention and redaction patterns under Resources ▸ Observability, and the private API's access model on Resources, API layer (api-private).

tables.name: Route key grammar
tables.note: One string drives file layout, the API path, IAM ARNs, the OpenAPI document and the handler's TypeScript type. Example: GET /v1/customer/vehicle/:id [private]
rows: pathParams: { id: string }, and no auth unless the route declares it

tables.name: What a thrown error becomes
tables.note: The error contract. Everything a handler can throw resolves to a deterministic status and telemetry event.
rows: domain_error_returned; logged at error for 5xx, warn otherwise

tables.name: Wildcard integrations
tables.note: A route ending in /* changes both the call signature and the IAM grant.
rows: the same, plus a required path appended to the base path
the ARN for that exact path
the ARN for the path prefix

d.role: Everything a domain team writes to ship a route: one config file for the domain and one handler file per route. No CDK, no IAM, no API Gateway.
facts: CODEOWNERS still assigns every path to the FLEX platform team, so this boundary is the intended operating model rather than today's ownership.

d.role: The CDK app reads the same config objects the Lambdas will read, and turns each route into a function, a method and a set of grants.
What runs inside every domain route Lambda, from cold start to API Gateway response.
The second, smaller SDK: one Lambda fronts one upstream system, with a route table instead of a filesystem convention.

zones.label: Declared in config · resolved per invocation

d.role: Two things a route declares by name and receives as a value: its resources and its feature flags.
The vocabulary every component emits and the logger it emits through.

The single declaration of a domain: its routes, resources, integrations, feature flags, headers, timeouts and the environments it deploys to. The CDK app reads it at synth and every route Lambda imports the same object at run time.
facts: domain(config) returns { config, route, routeContext }. Because the CDK app and the Lambda import the same module, there is no second description of a route to drift out of step.

Routes are keyed routes[version][path][METHOD][public|private], so one path and method can expose a public and a private variant with different schemas and headers — example's /v0/identity/:service does exactly that.
common holds the defaults every route inherits (access tier, log level, timeout, memory, headers); a route-level function block overrides them. With neither set the timeout is 15 seconds.

d.role: Turns the literal config object into the types each handler is checked against, so a mistyped resource key or route key is a compile error rather than a runtime throw.
facts: domain() is generic over its own argument: InferResourceKeys, InferIntegrationKeys, InferFeatureFlagKeys and InferEnvironmentKeys read the keys back out of the config, so a route may only list resources, integrations and flags that the same file defines.

The context type is built per route from the route key string and that route's schemas: ctx.pathParams.id exists because the key contains :id, and ctx.body takes its type from the route's body schema.

One field is keyed off the wrong axis. WithAuth adds ctx.auth unless the route's network access tier is public — which no domain uses — while at run time it is only populated for routes on the public gateway. Private routes therefore type-check against an auth object that is undefined when they run.

nodes.label: src/handlers/{version}/…
nodes.sub: one file per route · exports handler

d.role: The only per-route code a domain team writes: an async function that receives the typed context and returns a status with an optional payload.
facts: The file exports handler = route("GET /v1/customer/vehicles", fn). A private route carries the suffix [private] inside the route key and .private in its filename.
Throwing an http-errors error is the supported way to return a non-200: 5xx logs at error, 4xx at warn, and both emit domain_error_returned.
Code outside the handler reaches the same request context through routeContext{RouteKeys}() rather than passing it down as an argument.

nodes.label: One NodejsFunction per route
nodes.sub: plus its API Gateway method and grants

d.role: The domain stack walks the flattened route list and, for each entry, creates one Lambda, one API Gateway method and the grants that route alone needs.
facts: Public routes get a TokenAuthorizer pointed at the shared authorizer Lambda and are mounted at /app/{domain}/{version}{path}; private routes get AuthorizationType.IAM and are mounted at /domains/{domain}/{version}{path}.
Only the resources and integrations that route declares are granted to that route's role, so two routes in the same domain do not share permissions.
Every function is given FLEX_ENVIRONMENT set to the stage. STAGE is never set on a function, which is what breaks the feature-flag environment level.

nodes.label: flattenRoutes → toHandlerPath
nodes.sub: route key becomes a source path

d.role: The single rule that binds a config entry to a file on disk. It is the reason a domain needs no infrastructure code of its own.
facts: toHandlerPath builds handlers/{version}/{path}/{method}{ext}: the leading slash is dropped, each :param becomes a [param] directory, the method is lowercased, and the extension is .private.ts for a private-gateway route and .ts otherwise.
getDomainEntry prefixes domains/{name}/src/ and hands the result to NodejsFunction as its esbuild entry, so a route with no matching file fails at synth rather than at deploy.

getDeployableRoutes filters by the environments arrays, but getDeployableDomains returns every domain untouched for any non-persistent stage — which is why ephemeral and personal stages get the full route set.

d.role: The convention on three real dvla routes, including the two shapes that catch people out.
facts: GET /v1/customer/vehicle/:id becomes src/handlers/v1/customer/vehicle/[id]/get.ts — a square-bracket directory is a path parameter, and it is the only place the parameter name is declared.
POST /v1/unlink [private] becomes src/handlers/v1/unlink/post.private.ts. It has no ctx.auth, so it declares a required User-Id header instead.
The CDK construct id is the PascalCase of {domain}-{gateway}-{version}-{routeName}, and the same string becomes the logger's service name for that route.

nodes.label: route(key, handler)
nodes.sub: cold start · resolves the route config

d.role: Runs once per container: looks the route key up in the config, resolves log level, resources and headers, and builds the Middy stack around the core handler.
facts: Two phases: at module load it resolves the route config, log level, resources and header rules once, builds the Middy stack and memoises the integration invokers. Per invocation it only assembles the context and runs the handler.

The key is parsed back into method, version, path and gateway and used to look up routes[version][path][METHOD][gateway]. A key with no matching config entry throws at module load, before the first request.
The logger's service name is set here to {domain}-{gateway}-{version}-{routeName}, so every line a route logs identifies exactly which route wrote it.
logger.setLogLevel is a hard no-op when FLEX_ENVIRONMENT is production, so a route's declared log level has no effect in the one stage where raising it matters most.

d.tech: @middy/core with http-error-handler, http-header-normalizer, http-json-body-parser, secrets-manager and ssm
d.role: Wraps the core handler. Assembled once per container, and assembled conditionally from what the route declared.
facts: The header normaliser and JSON body parser are attached only for POST, PUT and PATCH; the Secrets Manager and SSM middlewares only when the route declares a resource of that type.
Both resource middlewares run with setToContext: true, so fetched values arrive on the Lambda context object rather than in the event.
injectLambdaContext is configured with correlationIdPath of headers."x-correlation-id", which is how the correlation id set at the edge reaches every domain log line.

nodes.label: Integrations
nodes.sub: one declaration · one call · one IAM statement

d.role: Turns each declared integration into a typed invoker on the context and, at synth, into the exact IAM statement that lets that one route make that one call.
facts: A declaration of { type, target, route } becomes the base path /domains/{target}/{version} or /gateways/{target}/{version} against the private API URL supplied by the route's ssm resource. The invokers and the signed fetcher are built once per container and cached.

At synth the same declaration becomes an execute-api:Invoke statement on that route's role, one statement per HTTP method, scoped to the method and path ARN. A route key ending /* is a wildcard the caller extends at call time, and the same * lands inside the IAM resource ARN.
Retries are opt-in and nothing opts in: DomainIntegrationBaseSchema has no retryAttempts field and no handler passes one at call time, so every domain-to-gateway call is a single attempt.
pnpm validate:integrations only checks type: "domain" integrations. A gateway integration naming a route the gateway does not define passes CI and 404s in production.

d.role: Validates the request and collects everything the route is allowed to see into one object.
facts: Body and query are Zod-parsed here; declared headers are only checked for presence, never against a schema, and a missing required header is a 400. A body schema on a GET route is ignored, because the body parser is only wired for POST, PUT and PATCH.
ctx.auth.pairwiseId is read from the API Gateway authorizer context and only for public-gateway routes; a missing pairwise id raises an authorization error.
Resources are split by type: kms and ssm are read straight from process.env, while secret and ssm:runtime are read off the Lambda context and throw if the middleware did not put them there.

d.role: Holds the assembled context for one invocation so any function in the call tree can reach it without it being threaded through arguments.
facts: The handler runs inside routeStorage.run(store, …) and is passed the same object as its typed context — the store and the context are one value, not a copy.
Service code calls routeContext{RouteKeys}() to get that store typed for the route keys it supports; calling it outside a handler throws rather than returning undefined.
The store carries only what the route declared: logger, auth, body, path and query params, resources, feature flags, headers and integrations.

d.role: Checks the handler's payload against the route's response schema and shapes the API Gateway result.
facts: A payload that fails the route's response schema is logged, emits response_validation_failed and is replaced by a 500 — the handler's payload is not returned.
Validation is skipped when the route declares no response schema or the handler returned no data, so an unschema'd route can return anything.
clearTmp() runs in a finally block on every invocation, deleting the contents of /tmp between reuses of a warm container.

d.role: The platform team's equivalent of domain.config.ts, one per upstream system: the routes FLEX exposes for it, the schemas it enforces, and the AWS resources the gateway may use.
facts: defineGateway(config) returns { config, createHandler } from the same module, so the declared route table and the handlers implementing it are type-checked against each other.
Route keys are flat METHOD /version/path strings with :param segments. There is no public or private split and no per-route access tier — the whole gateway is one function in one subnet tier.
Its resource types are a different set from a domain's: kms, role, secret and ssm. ssm throws "Not yet implemented" at synth, and no gateway config uses it.

d.role: Builds the gateway Lambda: the route table, the middleware and the closure over the config and the caller's route handlers.
facts: One NodejsFunction per gateway, wired to a single ANY /gateways/{name}/{proxy+} method on the private API with a 30-second timeout. The entire upstream surface sits behind that one method.
Its Middy stack is only injectLambdaContext with clearState: true — there is no error-handler middleware, so every error path runs through the handler's own catch.
logger.setLogLevel("INFO") is hard-coded: unlike a domain route, a gateway has no configurable log level.

nodes.label: lookupRoute
nodes.sub: strip the prefix, static then dynamic

d.role: Turns the proxied path back into one of the gateway's declared route keys before anything else runs.
facts: /gateways/{name} is stripped from the path first, then a static Map is tried by METHOD path, and only then the dynamic routes in declaration order, segment by segment.
An unmatched path and a matched route with no handler both return a 404 — which is exactly what a domain integration aimed at a route the gateway does not define receives.
A path with a trailing or duplicate slash fails the canonical-path check and is treated as unmatched.

d.role: Fetches and validates the gateway's consumer config on every invocation, before any client exists.
facts: Only secret resources resolve. kms, role and ssm are filtered out — they exist to drive IAM grants at synth and their values never reach the running code.

getSecret is called with maxAge: 600 and a JSON transform, so a warm container re-reads Secrets Manager at most every ten minutes and re-parses the result against the schema declared beside the resource.
A consumer config that stops matching its schema fails the request, not the deploy: the first invocation after the secret changes is the one that breaks.
The same pattern exists a second time as createConsumerConfigLoader in platform/shared, which nothing outside its own test imports.

d.role: The gateway's own module builds its upstream clients from the resolved config on every invocation; the route handler only ever sees the finished client.
facts: createRestClient with auth.type: "sigv4" assumes the upstream's consumer role through STS. The credential provider is memoised in a module-level Map keyed by role ARN and external id, so warm invocations reuse credentials until five minutes before expiry instead of calling AssumeRole every time.
createPublicFetch is the alternative — plain fetch with retryAttempts defaulting to 3, the only default retry anywhere in the platform.
An upstream 5xx becomes a flat 502 naming the gateway; an upstream 4xx is passed through with its body. A response that fails the route's schema is also a 502.

nodes.label: Feature flags
nodes.sub: four levels, one of them dead

d.role: Resolves each flag a route lists into a boolean on ctx.featureFlags, once per invocation.
facts: Order: process.env[key] equal to the string "true" or "false" wins; otherwise the flag is true if its environments list contains the current environment; otherwise its default; otherwise false.
Levels two and three are an OR rather than a fallback chain, so an environments list can switch a flag on for one stage but can never switch it off when default is true.

The environment level does not work in a deployed Lambda. The current environment is read from process.env.STAGE, and no Flex function construct sets STAGE — only FLEX_ENVIRONMENT — so it falls back to development in every stage, production included.
Nothing injects a flag override variable either: an override has to be written by hand into the route's or the domain's function.environment block.
code: env vars a function actually gets

d.tech: SSM Parameter Store · Secrets Manager · KMS · Middy
d.role: The declaration looks identical for all four types; when the value materialises does not, and that split is what the isolated tier's endpoint list has to satisfy.
facts: Deploy time: ssm puts the parameter's value straight into the env var and kms puts the key ARN there. Both are readable from process.env the moment the function starts.

Run time: secret puts the secret name into the env var and ssm:runtime puts the parameter name, and the Middy middlewares fetch the real value onto the Lambda context. That is why an isolated-tier function needs the Secrets Manager and SSM interface endpoints at all.
The env var name is the config key itself — declare udpNotificationSecret and the function gets an env var of that name — and the CDK grant is attached to that one route's role for that one resource.
scope: "stage" prefixes the parameter path with the stage name instead of the environment name, which is how an ephemeral stage reads its own private API URL.

nodes.label: @flex/telemetry
nodes.sub: 21 events in five groups, plus 3 for the edge

d.tech: Zod enum over a log line
d.role: The closed vocabulary every component emits, and the layer you actually query when tracing a request through the platform.
facts: TelemetryEventSchema is a closed Zod enum of 21 events in five groups — auth (6), domain (3), service gateway (4), third party (5) and general (3). Adding an event means editing the enum.

CloudFront Functions get their own three-event registry (cff_token_validated, cff_token_missing, cff_token_invalid) behind the separate @flex/telemetry/cff export, deliberately outside the Zod enum because zod will not fit in a CloudFront Function bundle.

An event is not a metric: emitTelemetry is a single logger.info("telemetry", …) call, so everything arrives as a log line rather than EMF. The CloudFront Function version writes the identical shape with console.log.
The two halves of one call are emitted by different components: the domain's invoker emits service_gateway_request_sent and the gateway Lambda emits service_gateway_request_received.

nodes.label: @flex/logging
nodes.sub: the logger everything else writes through

d.tech: @aws-lambda-powertools/logger with a Flex formatter and sanitiser
d.role: One shared logger instance: structured JSON, a per-route service name, the correlation id from the edge, and a redacting JSON replacer.
facts: FlexLogger overrides setLogLevel to return early when FLEX_ENVIRONMENT is production, so the level cannot be raised there at all.

The redacting replacer is installed at construction as jsonReplacerFn, which is why it applies to every log line rather than only to ones written through a helper. Retention and the redaction patterns themselves are covered under Resources ▸ Observability.

d.carries: The route table, filtered by the environments arrays
facts: The CDK app imports the same domain.config.ts the Lambda will import, so no route list is written twice.

edges.label: every route needs an entry file
the file the team must have written

facts: If the file is missing, NodejsFunction fails at synth — the route is never deployed half-wired.

d.carries: resource, integration, flag and environment keys
the shape of ctx for this exact route

edges.label: first thing the core handler does

facts: buildDomainIntegrations is wrapped in cache(), so the signed fetcher and the invokers are built once per container.

d.carries: logger, auth, body, params, resources, flags, headers, integrations

d.auth: SigV4 with the route Lambda's own execution role
d.carries: The integration's base path plus any wildcard suffix
facts: Signed with the calling Lambda's own credentials, not an assumed role — the assumed role appears one hop later, between the gateway and its upstream.
Single attempt: nothing on this path sets retryAttempts.

d.carries: strings — a value, an ARN or a fetched secret
the route key, its schemas and the parsed request
apiUrl, apiKey, consumer role ARN, region, external id
facts: The client factory receives only resolved secrets, so a gateway handler never touches an ARN or an env var.

d.carries: event name plus a small details object
event name plus a small details object
